title: T1586 — Compromise Accounts
subtitle: Watch the full story of one account takeover, from a stolen password list to the response.
aria: Animated diagram of the attack story. A full text version follows in the written steps below.

steps.title: Buy stolen credentials
steps.caption: The attacker buys a list of stolen usernames and passwords from a stealer-log market.
steps.defender: Nothing yet. The sale happens in criminal forums, outside company systems.

fields.detail: The attacker buys a list of stolen usernames and passwords from a stealer-log market.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Test passwords on the login page
steps.caption: The attacker tries the stolen passwords against the company sign-in page, spread over days and many IP addresses.
steps.defender: A burst of failed sign-ins appears in IdP logs. The burst is often spread over days and many IP addresses.

fields.detail: The attacker tries the stolen passwords against the company sign-in page, spread over days and many

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Push MFA prompts until someone approves
steps.caption: The attacker keeps sending approval requests to the user's phone.
steps.defender: A storm of MFA push requests shows up. Many users approve just to stop the noise (MFA fatigue).

fields.detail: The attacker keeps sending approval requests to the user's phone.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: The user approves - attacker gets a session
steps.caption: The user taps approve by mistake. The attacker now holds a valid session.
steps.defender: A sign-in from a new country and device appears next to the user's normal pattern (impossible travel).

fields.detail: The user taps approve by mistake. The attacker now holds a valid session.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Enroll a rogue MFA device and set an inbox rule
steps.caption: The attacker adds their own MFA device and creates a hidden inbox rule.
steps.defender: A new MFA device is registered and an inbox rule is created. These are high-value alerts.

fields.detail: The attacker adds their own MFA device and creates a hidden inbox rule.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Send phishing from the trusted account
steps.caption: The attacker uses the trusted mailbox to phish the user's colleagues.
steps.defender: Unusual send volume and new external recipients from a trusted mailbox.

fields.detail: The attacker uses the trusted mailbox to phish the user's colleagues.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Reset passwords on other services
steps.caption: Password-reset emails from other services land in the mailbox and are used to widen the takeover.
steps.defender: Password-reset emails and notices leave the mailbox for other services.

fields.detail: Password-reset emails from other services land in the mailbox and are used to widen the takeover.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC responds
steps.caption: The SOC revokes sessions, resets credentials, and removes the rogue device.
steps.defender: Sessions are revoked, MFA is re-enrolled, and the user is re-educated. Evidence is kept for review.

fields.detail: The SOC revokes sessions, resets credentials, and removes the rogue device.

detection.label: Contained
detection.detail: The activity is contained and the lesson is captured.
